brief_summary: Line chart of travel depth over time for a single keystroke. A coral curve descends to a peak, marks an actuation crossing, rises partway (marked with a reset-delta bracket), re-actuates mid-stroke without returning to rest, then fully releases. A dashed grey horizontal line marks a fixed actuation point for comparison, labeled as where a contact-closure switch commits and nowhere else.
data_sources: rapid-trigger-firmware-deep-dive.mdx § 'Reset distance is the whole feature' — 'a partial release that doesn't cross back past the actuation point never registers at all... On a rapid-trigger switch, the same partial lift clears the reset delta long before the stem gets anywhere near the top of the stroke, the key releases, and a re-press a fraction of a millimetre later re-actuates immediately.'

rapid-trigger-firmware-deep-dive.mdx § 'Why a contact closure can't run this loop at all' — 'The leaf snaps against the terminal at a fixed point in the stem's travel — the actuation point cut into the housing.'
warnings: Curve geometry is schematic (illustrative stroke shape), not measured sensor data — no specific mm/gauss values are plotted, consistent with the no-fabrication discipline.
